subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Caffeine and the Heart
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Caffeine and the Heart.

hook.text: For decades, doctors warned that coffee was bad for the heart. The science now tells a different story.

buildup.text: Caffeine temporarily raises heart rate and blood pressure—about 3–5 mmHg for a few hours after drinking.

discovery.text: Large studies show moderate coffee drinkers (3–5 cups/day) have lower risk of heart disease than non-drinkers.

twist.text: The antioxidants and polyphenols in coffee may outweigh the temporary cardiovascular stimulation caffeine causes.

climax.text: People with certain gene variants (slow CYP1A2 metabolizers) may face higher heart risk from heavy coffee intake.

punchline.text: Moderate coffee is heart-friendly for most. Genetics set the individual limit.

quiz.question: What do large studies show about moderate coffee consumption and heart disease?
options: Moderate drinkers have lower risk than non-drinkers

details.summary: Moderate caffeine consumption has a neutral to mildly protective effect on heart health for most people. It temporarily raises blood pressure and heart rate, but habitual drinkers develop tolerance to these effects. Recent meta-analyses link moderate intake to reduced cardiovascular risk.
details.whyItMatters: For decades people worried coffee was bad for the heart. Modern evidence largely reverses that concern, making it important to separate myth from current science.
takeaways: Moderate caffeine intake is neutral to mildly protective for hearts
Temporary blood pressure spikes diminish with regular consumption
Meta-analyses associate three to five cups daily with lower CV risk

faq.question: Should people with high blood pressure avoid caffeine entirely?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Habitual coffee drinkers develop tolerance to the blood pressure effect. However, those with uncontrolled hypertension should consult their doctor, especially if they are slow caffeine metabolizers.

faq.question: Does caffeine cause heart palpitations or arrhythmias?
faq.answer: Large studies show moderate caffeine intake does not increase arrhythmia risk in most people. Some individuals with pre-existing conditions may experience palpitations, but for the general population the risk is minimal.
